text:
maria: Heads up — canary for NF4+FP4 mix (region us-west-2) showing a weird throughput drop and a KV cache memory spike ~30m after rollout. p95 up ~18%, some hosts hit OOMs on small-host pool. deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-18T10:04Z -> rev nf4-fp4-mix-2026-03-18 (10%)
kevin: OOMs? which hosts, logs? any kernel swap messages?
maria: host ids: hw-gpu-34/35/42. dmesg: "oom_reaper" triggered, docker shim restarted. No explicit kernel swap but runtime logs show slowpath fallback for some layers.
sophie: slowpath fallback usually implies kernel selection chose a non-inlined kernel for some 4-bit ops. Could be calibration produced weight scales that trigger int8 fallback?
ryan: I pulled a perf trace from hw-gpu-34 — top of stack:
```
# perf top sample
runtime::execute_attention
quant_kernels::nf4_conv_forward (slowpath)
batching::schedule_dispatch
kv_cache::alloc_fragment
```
And nvprof shows a sudden spike in small memcpy calls.
anil: small memcpy spike + alloc_fragment smells like KV cache fragmentation + tiny microbatches. Did batching heuristics change in the canary?
maria: batching config is same, but the model profile changed: avg seq len dropped ~10% which increased microbatching frequency. We also applied per-tensor calibration from the new quant pack.
kevin: if calibration shifted scales per-layer, kernels that were previously vectorized could now take slow scalar kernels. Need per-layer kernel mapping + a quick histogram of scale values.
sophie: can we reproduce on a non-prod host? If we feed the same input-distribution and old/new calibration we can compare kernel selection traces.
ryan: repro started: ran 50 requests mimicking traffic. With new calib repo I see kernel decision matrix: layer 12/14 chose fp4->nf4 mixed kernel fallback to generic_int4_slow. With old calib they used optimized_nf4_avx.
kevin: That explains perf. Why memory spike then?
ryan: the slow kernel uses a different temporary buffer pattern: it allocates per microbatch instead of reusing KV segments. Under microbatch-heavy workload that fragments the KV slab, triggering many small heap allocations -> fragmentation -> OOM after ~30m.
anil: tl;dr: calibration altered scale ranges -> kernel lookup picked slow path -> different buffer lifecycle -> KV fragmentation -> OOM.
maria: summary is great. Options: rollback canary, force kernel mapping override for affected layers, or re-run calibration with clipping to original dynamic range. Thoughts?
kevin: immediate -> rollback canary for safety. Next -> add guard in runtime: for kernel selection prefer optimized kernels if their perf difference < threshold and memory pattern is compatible.
sophie: Agreed. Also add a fast telemetry hook: when kernel decision flips between optimized and slow for same layer+shape increase an alert counter.
ryan: I'll snapshot the stack and perf traces and open a bisect PR to map which calibration commit triggered the change.
maria: Deploy-bot, please rollback canary to baseline nf4-only in us-west-2.
deploy-bot: initiating rollback -> rollback job id rb-2101112222-1 started.
kevin: can we add a temporary routing policy to route heavy microbatch traffic to dedicated pool until we fix calibration? Don't want cross-tenant OOMs.
anil: yes, we have a routing flag. I'll flip it for traffic tag "short-seq-heavy".
sophie: also we should add a quick unit test in CI that compares kernel selection matrices between quant packs for a handful of representative inputs. If selection diverges, fail the pack until triaged.
maria: action items: 1) rollback canary (done by bot) 2) ryan bisect calibration repo -> PR #? 3) anil enable routing flag 4) kevin runtime guard + telemetry 5) sophie CI kernel-selection test. Assign owners and ETA?
ryan: I'll have bisect PR WIP in ~3h.
anil: routing flag flipped in 5m.
kevin: I'll prototype kernel-selection guard and a perf test today, aiming for EOD.
sophie: CI test sketch in a GH issue, will fill details by EOD.
maria: thanks everyone. Leaving logs and perf dumps in /mnt/rt/perf/2101112222 (link: https://internal.perf/2101112222). Reopen thread if rollback shows residual issues. :white_check_mark:
